title: Quick check: Adding React to an Existing Website

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Adding React to an Existing Website”?
options: The concept allows application code to mutate React-managed DOM and state directly.
Understanding incremental adoption should be justified by requirements, acceptance criteria, tests, and explicit trade-offs.
The concept removes the need to consider error states or accessibility.
The browser will infer all application behavior even if inputs and state are contradictory.
questions.answer_key: Understanding incremental adoption should be justified by requirements, acceptance criteria, tests, and explicit trade-offs.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Adding React to an Existing Website: Understanding incremental adoption should be justified by requirements, acceptance criteria, tests, and explicit trade-offs.

questions.prompt: Which practice is most reliable when applying Understanding incremental adoption?
options: Document what is in scope, what is out of scope, and how reviewers can reproduce the result.
Skip validation because a successful render proves that the application is correct.
Store duplicate copies of every value so each component can change it independently.
Optimize by adding every available Hook without measuring the result.
questions.answer_key: Document what is in scope, what is out of scope, and how reviewers can reproduce the result.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Adding React to an Existing Website: Document what is in scope, what is out of scope, and how reviewers can reproduce the result.

questions.prompt: What should you verify before considering “Adding React to an Existing Website” complete?
options: Check only whether the file exists; syntax and runtime behavior do not matter.
Assume a client-side check proves that a remote service accepted the change.
Rely only on a screenshot of the happy path and never repeat the test.
Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
questions.answer_key: Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Adding React to an Existing Website: Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
